description:
FILED s521 (Fable, 2026-10-18 17:4x) from the ROUND-1 COMPANION on MAIN-READY-32 (review/companion-r1.log: op/fork.t 24/4 -> 23/5, FIXED 1 + LOST 1 on the SAME description key) and its follow-ups: alone on main (review/fork-r1.log) 23/5 in the parallel AND the serial pass; the bisect over the MAIN-READY-26..31 code extractions (review/bisect-fork.log, review/bisect-fork.sh): 24/4 on ff4c1500, a074452f, fca3593b, fd04c048; 23/5 on 5e6e241d and a5885afc -- BUT the 5e6e241d leg's own journal (base-5e6e241d/.suitelog/run-journal.tsv) holds 23/5 for its first run and 24/4 for the serial re-run of the same file: the fifth failure is NOT deterministic.  Verdict: a FLAPPER that appeared with s519b (MAIN-READY-30), like io/pvbm.t's -- NOT re-blessed (re-blessing a flapper only moves which run looks wrong, DECIDED s470bv); the snapshot row stays 24/4 with the flap noted in its cause column.

WHAT IS KNOWN: t/op/fork.t is `run_multiple_progs('', \*DATA)` -- 28 child programs (separated by ########), each run through the child perl (PCL via tools/pclperl-for-tests) and compared; every row's description is the same `[at t/op/fork.t line 18]` (the one-key trap, #1041), so the FIXED / LOST buckets cannot name the case; the four deterministic failures are perl rows 14, 15, 16, 22 (#1770).  s519b's changes that a fork+pipe child could feel: `%p-glob-io-key` (`*A = *STDOUT` aliases the real handle), `%p-load-text-stream` (the uncached module load path), p-declare-sub's section-head reservation (an emission change on every module), the Test::Builder bridge -- none obviously timing-related; a flap smells like output-flush ORDER between parent and child on a shared fd (the #3327 family: the s521b brief's member 4), or a waitpid / exit-status race.

HOW TO IDENTIFY: run the 28 cases one by one (split the DATA section; each case names its expected output after `EXPECT`) under PCL via `tools/pclperl-for-tests`, ten times each, on main; the case whose result varies is the flapper; then diff its output against perl's and read the mechanism.  Bar: the case named, its reproducer vs perl in this task, a fix if ONE mechanism (then the row leaves perl-suite-fails.tsv / the snapshot moves by edit), else the flap registered with its cause in perl-suite-run.tsv's cause column.  LOW: one row; the file is fork-heavy and has a contention history.


=== IDENTIFIED (s521d, Opus 5.5, 2026-10-18) -- NOT FIXED: the fix needs a ruling ===
THE CASE: t/op/fork.t DATA case 9 (OPTION random):
    $| = 1; $\ = "\n";
    fork() ? do { require Config; print($Config::Config{osname} eq $^O); }
           : do { require Config; print($Config::Config{osname} eq $^O); }
Run 10 times under tools/pclperl-for-tests (every one of the 27 cases, ten runs each, scratch/s521d/fork/ in the s521d worktree): case 9 passes 6 of 10; every other case is stable (cases 10, 14, 15, 16, 22 fail 10 of 10 = the deterministic fails; all others 10 of 10).  The failing runs print `1` once and then `Failed to transpile .../lib/5.40.3/Exporter.pm`.
THE MECHANISM (measured with labelled variants, scratch/s521d/fork/c09b-d.pl): it is always the CHILD that fails, and only when the PARENT does not wait -- with `waitpid($p, 0)` in the parent the variant is 12 of 12.  pclperl-for-tests loads Pl/t/PCLCore.pm, which sets PCL_XSERVER (the #1545 transpile server) OWNED by the wrapper perl ($$, its tempdir, its END unlinks the socket and capture files; the server _exits within a second of its owner).  The child SBCL outlives the parent SBCL; the wrapper exits as soon as the parent does, tearing the server down while the child's `require Config` -> `pl2cl --module Exporter.pm` is in flight -> the client reports the failed reply as a failed transpile.  A child that requires AFTER the teardown falls back to the plain path but prints `pl2cl: PCL_XSERVER=... names no existing directory` on stderr (c09d) -- the same race's other face, also an output mismatch under 2>&1.  Not a PCL fork bug: perl's child runs the same program fine; it is the HARNESS server's lifetime vs a fork child that outlives the program's main process.  Why since MAIN-READY-30 is not established (s519b's uncached-loader change is the obvious candidate for moving the window, not for the mechanism).
FIX OPTIONS (a ruling): (1) pclperl-for-tests does not hand its own short-lived server to the program it runs (PCL_XSERVER= for the SBCL it starts: every child pays the plain pl2cl spawn per module -- a companion SPEED cost, measure first); (2) the server's owner becomes the outer harness's (an inherited PCL_XSERVER is reused, not replaced) -- still a race for a grandchild that outlives the outer test; (3) pl2cl's client treats a reply cut off by the server's own exit as "no server" and falls back (the client already does that for a missing socket; it would need the server to mark an owner-exit reply distinctly, never a real transpile failure).  Until ruled: perl-suite-run.tsv's op/fork.t row (24/4, NOT re-blessed) carries this cause.

=== RULED (Fable, s521, 2026-10-18 20:1x; DECIDED ## s521) === Option (3): pl2cl's transpile-server CLIENT treats a reply cut off by the server's own exit (EOF / a closed connection before a complete reply) as "no server" and FALLS BACK to the plain path SILENTLY -- exactly as it already does for a missing socket -- and the `pl2cl: PCL_XSERVER=... names no existing directory` stderr line goes the same way (a harness detail must never reach a program's stderr: the sweep compares 2>&1).  A real transpile failure is a COMPLETE reply with an error status, so the two are distinguishable without a server-side marker; if the protocol cannot tell them apart today, the server writes a one-byte status before the body and the client requires it.  Options (1) and (2) are rejected: (1) costs every child a plain pl2cl spawn per module (a companion speed cost the harness should not pay), (2) leaves the race for a grandchild.  Scheduled in the parked s521e brief (`s521/s521e-prompt.md`, member 5).  BAR: op/fork.t DATA case 9 twelve of twelve under tools/pclperl-for-tests without a waitpid; `tools/run-perl-suite.pl --jobs 1 op/fork.t` 24/4 three times; a tools/t/ row that kills the server mid-reply and sees a silent fallback; the companion's op/fork.t row loses its flap note.
